risk_if_not_implemented: Without Geographic Data Location, sensitive and/or regulated data may be disclosed, altered or lost through inadequate classification, handling or protection. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Unauthorized Retention / Inability to Dispose of Data (R-AM-3), Unaddressed Security / Compliance Exposure (R-GV-2), Inability to Demonstrate Due Diligence / Due Care (R-GV-9), and most likely increases susceptibility to Human Error (MT-9), Data Quality Degradation / Data Poisoning (MT-12).

compensating_control_1.name: Geolocation Requirements for Processing, Storage and Service Locations
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to control the location of Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) processing and/or storage based on business requirements that includes statutory, regulatory and contractual obligations.
compensating_control_1.justification: Geolocation Requirements for Processing, Storage and Service Locations (DCH-30.1) provides overlapping security capability that compensates for the absence of Geographic Location of Data (DCH-30) by addressing related risk objectives through an alternative control mechanism aligned with Data applicability. Given the data-handling focus of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Data Localization
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to constrain the impact of "digital sovereignty laws," that require localized data within the host country, where data and processes may be subjected to arbitrary enforcement actions that potentially violate other applicable statutory, regulatory and/or contractual obligations.
compensating_control_2.justification: Data Localization (DCH-31) provides overlapping security capability that compensates for the absence of Geographic Location of Data (DCH-30) by addressing related risk objectives through an alternative control mechanism aligned with Data applicability. Given the data-handling focus of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
